solution.full_text:
1. The correct answer is option (3).
2. Some lipids have phosphorous and a phosphorylated organic compound in them. These are phospholipids. They are found in cell membrane. Lecithin is one example.
3. Option (4) is incorrect as glycerides are another group of lipids in which both glycerol and fatty acids are present.
4. Option (1) and (2) are incorrect as carbohydrates and amino acids are separate groups of biomolecules.

chapter.name: Anatomy of Flowering Plants
chapter.why: The answer depends on the role of bulliform cells in the epidermis of monocot (isobilateral) leaves, which curl leaves inward; this is taught in Anatomy of Flowering Plants.

subtopics.name: Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Leaf
subtopics.why: The answer depends on bulliform cells of the monocot (grass) leaf epidermis becoming flaccid under water stress so the leaf curls inward, which is taught under the monocotyledonous leaf.

examtopicmapping_subtopics.name: Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Leaf
examtopicmapping_subtopics.why: The answer depends on bulliform cells of the monocot (grass) leaf epidermis becoming flaccid under water stress so the leaf curls inward, which is taught under the monocotyledonous leaf.

solution.full_text:
1. In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells.
2. These are called bulliform cells.
3. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed.
4. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

chapter.name: Structural Organisation in Animals
chapter.why: The answer depends on the external morphology of cockroach (anal cerci on the 10th abdominal segment), which is taught under the cockroach section of Structural Organisation in Animals.

subtopics.name: Morphology of Cockroach
subtopics.why: The answer depends on the external body segmentation of the cockroach, where anal cerci arise from the 10th abdominal segment, which is external morphology.

examtopicmapping_subtopics.name: Morphology of Cockroach
examtopicmapping_subtopics.why: The answer depends on the external body segmentation of the cockroach, where anal cerci arise from the 10th abdominal segment, which is external morphology.

solution.full_text:
1. Correct answer is option (3), because in both sexes of cockroach, $10^{\mathrm{th}}$ segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci.
2. Options (1), (2) and (4) are incorrect because $5^{\mathrm{th}}$, $8^{\mathrm{th}}$ and $9^{\mathrm{th}}$ segments do not bear such structures.
3. In adult cockroaches only $10^{\mathrm{th}}$ segments are present in abdomen.
4. $11^{\mathrm{th}}$ abdominal segment is absent.

  3. In adult cockroaches only 10th segments are present in abdomen.

subtopics.name: Muscle Tissue and Neural Tissue
subtopics.why: The answer depends on identifying skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle fibres from their structure and matching each to its location in the body, which is taught under muscle tissue.

examtopicmapping_subtopics.name: Muscle Tissue and Neural Tissue
examtopicmapping_subtopics.why: The answer depends on identifying skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle fibres from their structure and matching each to its location in the body, which is taught under muscle tissue.

solution.full_text:
1. The correct answer is option (3) as
2. Figure (a) represents skeletal muscle fibres which are closely attached to skeletal bones.
3. In a typical muscle such as triceps and biceps, striated muscle fibres are bundled together in a parallel fashion.
4. Figure (b) represents smooth muscle fibres which are present in the wall of internal organs such as the blood vessels, stomach and intestine.
5. Figure (c) represents cardiac muscle fibres which are exclusively present in the heart.
